items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Harper (phonetic sp.) played more changes, but I did that [sings], but man, that Harper [sings], he was whipping in between those changes.

ctx.x: Like, man, I dug Lester Young (phonetic sp.), but Harper (phonetic sp.) played more changes, but I did that [sings], but man, that Harper [sings], he was whipping in between those changes. But see, that's, that's the thing. You have to live and learn and find out because the things that you think are great today like won't be too cool tomorrow. There's always something a little better, you know, if you're looking in the right direction, you know. But things that -- you know, there's always something better if…

When you were a young player coming up and you were listening to other players and listening to recordings of other players, did you also have the opportunity to go to jam sessions and try to learn that way as well?
